claim: Cdc7 kinase is required for initiation of DNA replication at replication origins.
source: Cdc7 kinase, required for initiation of DNA replication at replication origins, has been implicated in checkpoint activation but how it is involved in this pathway has not been known.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Cdc7 is required for Claspin-Chk1 interaction in human cancer cells.
source: Here, we show that Cdc7 is required for Claspin-Chk1 interaction in human cancer cells by phosphorylating CKBD (Chk1-binding-domain) of Claspin.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: Cdc7 phosphorylates CKBD (Chk1-binding-domain) of Claspin.
source: Here, we show that Cdc7 is required for Claspin-Chk1 interaction in human cancer cells by phosphorylating CKBD (Chk1-binding-domain) of Claspin.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 4 and in vitro kinase assays in Figure 6.

claim: The residual Chk1 activation in Cdc7-depleted cells is lost upon further depletion of casein kinase1 (CK1γ1).
source: The residual Chk1 activation in Cdc7-depleted cells is lost upon further depletion of casein kinase1 (CK1γ1), previously reported to phosphorylate CKBD.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 5A.

claim: CK1γ1 was previously reported to phosphorylate CKBD.
source: The residual Chk1 activation in Cdc7-depleted cells is lost upon further depletion of casein kinase1 (CK1γ1), previously reported to phosphorylate CKBD.
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge from the literature, specifically referencing work by Dunphy's group (Meng et al., 2011).

claim: Cdc7, in conjunction with CK1γ1, facilitates the interaction between Claspin and Chk1 through phosphorylating CKBD.
source: Thus, Cdc7, in conjunction with CK1γ1, facilitates the interaction between Claspin and Chk1 through phosphorylating CKBD.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental findings shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Cdc7 is predominantly responsible for CKBD phosphorylation in cancer cells.
source: We also show that, whereas Cdc7 is predominantly responsible for CKBD phosphorylation in cancer cells, CK1γ1 plays a major role in non-cancer cells, providing rationale for targeting Cdc7 for cancer cell-specific cell killing.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 5A, 5B, and 7.

claim: CK1γ1 plays a major role in CKBD phosphorylation in non-cancer cells.
source: We also show that, whereas Cdc7 is predominantly responsible for CKBD phosphorylation in cancer cells, CK1γ1 plays a major role in non-cancer cells, providing rationale for targeting Cdc7 for cancer cell-specific cell killing.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claim: Cdc7 kinase plays a crucial role in initiation of DNA replication by phosphorylating Mcm proteins.
source: Cdc7 kinase plays a crucial role in initiation of DNA replication by phosphorylating Mcm proteins, essential as a part of the replicative helicase (Masai and Arai, 2002; Masai et al., 2010; Labib, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Inhibition of DNA replication by hydroxyl urea (HU) or UV triggers cellular responses known as replication stress checkpoint.
source: Inhibition of DNA replication by hydroxyl urea (HU) or UV triggers cellular responses known as replication stress checkpoint (Branzei and Foiani, 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: ATR-mediated phosphorylation of Chk1 requires Claspin as a mediator/adaptor for the signal transfer.
source: ATR-mediated phosphorylation of Chk1 requires Clapsin as a mediator/adaptor for the signal transfer.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: ATR phosphorylates Chk1 in the Claspin-Chk1 complex more efficiently than Chk1 alone in the absence of Claspin in vitro.
source: Indeed, ATR phosphorylates Chk1 in the Clapsin-Chk1 complex more efficiently than Chk1 alone in the absence of Claspin in virto (Lindsey-Boltz et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge supported by a citation to Lindsey-Boltz et al., 2009.

claim: In budding yeast, Rad53 checkpoint effector kinase directly phosphorylates Dbf4 upon fork stalling to block late origin firing.
source: In budding yeast, it is known that Rad53 checkpoint effector kinase directly phosphorylates Dbf4 upon fork stalling to block late origin firing most likely through inhibition of the Cdc7 kinase function (Zegerman and Diffley, 2010; Lopez-Mosqueda et al., 2010; Duch et al., 2011), although the mechanism of this regulation is not clear (Weinreich and Stillman, 1999).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In mammalian cells, Cdc7 was implicated in repair of stalled replication forks through Rad18.
source: In mammalian cells, it was implicated in repair of stalled replication forks through Rad18 (Day et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge supported by a citation to Day et al., 2010.

claim: In fission yeast, activation of checkpoint kinase was impaired in cdc7 mutant cells.
source: In fission yeast, activation of checkpoint kinase was impaired in cdc7 mutant cells (Shimmoto et al., 2009; Matsumoto et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge supported by citations to Shimmoto et al., 2009 and Matsumoto et al., 2010.

claim: The impaired checkpoint activation in cdc7 bypass mutants provided strong evidence that Cdc7 is required for checkpoint activation in yeasts.
source: However, the impaired checkpoint activation in cdc7 bypass mutants (∆mcm4N ∆cdc7 in budding yeast and rif1∆ hsk1∆ in fission yeast; Sheu and Stillman, 2010; Hayano et al., 2011; Ogi et al., 2008; our unpublished data) provided strong evidence that Cdc7 is required for checkpoint activation in yeasts.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from prior studies supported by citations and unpublished data.

claim: Induced knockout of Cdc7 gene in mouse ES cells resulted in almost complete loss of Chk1 activation in response to HU or UV irradiation.
source: In mammalian cells, induced knockout of Cdc7 gene in mouse ES cells as well as siRNA-mediated inhibition of Cdc7 expression in cancer cells resulted in almost complete loss of Chk1 activation in response to HU or UV irradiation (Kim et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge supported by a citation to Kim et al., 2008.

claim: siRNA-mediated inhibition of Cdc7 expression in cancer cells resulted in almost complete loss of Chk1 activation in response to HU or UV irradiation.
source: In mammalian cells, induced knockout of Cdc7 gene in mouse ES cells as well as siRNA-mediated inhibition of Cdc7 expression in cancer cells resulted in almost complete loss of Chk1 activation in response to HU or UV irradiation (Kim et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge supported by a citation to Kim et al., 2008.

claim: Requirement of Cdc7 for timely checkpoint activation in cancer cells was confirmed by using a compound that inhibits Cdc7 kinase.
source: Later, requirement of Cdc7 for timely checkpoint activation in cancer cells was confirmed by using a compound that inhibits Cdc7 kinase (Rainey et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge supported by a citation to Rainey et al., 2013.

claim: Replication stress-induced hyperphosphorylation of Claspin/Mrc1 is largely gone in cells where Cdc7 activity is compromised.
source: Furthermore, replication stress-induced hyperphosphorylation of Claspin/Mrc1 exemplified by mobility-shift on PAGE is largely gone in cells where Cdc7 activity is compromised (Kim et al., 2008; Shimmoto et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge supported by citations to Kim et al., 2008 and Shimmoto et al., 2009.

claim: Claspin was originally discovered as a factor that binds to Chk1 in Xenopus egg extract.
source: Claspin, originally discovered as a factor that binds to Chk1 in Xenopus egg extract (Kumagai and Dunphy, 2000), and its yeast homologue, Mrc1, are essential for activation of downstream effector kinases (Chk1 and Cds1/Rad53, respectively), and are required for replication checkpoint control as a mediator (Chini and Chen, 2003; Yoo et al., 2006; Lindsey-Boltz et al., 2009; Alcasabas et al., 2001; Osborn and Elledge, 2003; Tanaka and Russell, 2001).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation to Kumagai and Dunphy, 2000.

claim: Claspin and its yeast homologue Mrc1 are essential for activation of downstream effector kinases.
source: Claspin, originally discovered as a factor that binds to Chk1 in Xenopus egg extract (Kumagai and Dunphy, 2000), and its yeast homologue, Mrc1, are essential for activation of downstream effector kinases (Chk1 and Cds1/Rad53, respectively), and are required for replication checkpoint control as a mediator (Chini and Chen, 2003; Yoo et al., 2006; Lindsey-Boltz et al., 2009; Alcasabas et al., 2001; Osborn and Elledge, 2003; Tanaka and Russell, 2001).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Claspin/Mrc1 is required for efficient fork progression.
source: Claspin/Mrc1 is required also for efficient fork progression (Lin et al., 2004; Petermann et al., 2008; Scorah and McGowan, 2009; Szyjka et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Yeast Mrc1 was shown to move along with replication fork, linking the helicase components to the replicative polymerases.
source: Yeast Mrc1 was shown to move along with replication fork, linking the helicase components to the replicative polymerases (Katou et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge supported by a citation to Katou et al., 2003.

claim: Mrc1, in conjunction with Tof1/Csm3, was shown to stimulate DNA replication fork progression in an in vitro reconstitution assay system.
source: More recently, Mrc1, in conjunction with Tof1/Csm3, was shown to stimulate DNA replication fork progression in an in vitro reconstitution assay system (Yeeles et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge supported by a citation to Yeeles et al., 2017.

claim: Claspin has a novel role as a recruiter of Cdc7 kinase for efficient phosphorylation of Mcm proteins required for initiation.
source: We recently reported a novel role of Claspin as a recruiter of Cdc7 kinase for efficient phosphorylation of Mcm proteins required for initiation (Yang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge from the authors' own work, supported by a citation to Yang et al., 2016.

claim: In Xenopus egg extracts, conserved serine-864 and serine-895 are phosphorylated upon replication stress and this phosphorylation is required for checkpoint activation.
source: In Xenopus egg extracts, conserved serine-864 and serine-895 are phosphorylated upon replication stress and this phosphorylation is required for checkpoint activation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: CKBD is required for checkpoint activation in Xenopus.
source: CKBD is required for checkpoint activation, and a phosphopeptide containing CKBD is sufficient for binding to Chk1.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: A phosphopeptide containing CKBD is sufficient for binding to Chk1.
source: CKBD is required for checkpoint activation, and a phosphopeptide containing CKBD is sufficient for binding to Chk1.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: In human cells, Thr-916 residue in CKBD was reported to be phosphorylated in response to HU.
source: In human cells, Thr-916 residue in CKBD was reported to be phosphorylated in response to HU and the 3A mutant (T916A S945A S983A) is deficient in checkpoint activation (Chini and Chen, 2006).
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge supported by a citation to Chini and Chen, 2006.

claim: The 3A mutant (T916A S945A S983A) of Claspin is deficient in checkpoint activation.
source: In human cells, Thr-916 residue in CKBD was reported to be phosphorylated in response to HU and the 3A mutant (T916A S945A S983A) is deficient in checkpoint activation (Chini and Chen, 2006).
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge supported by a citation to Chini and Chen, 2006.

claim: Chk1 kinase was reported to phosphorylate Thr-916 in vitro.
source: Chk1 kinase was reported to phosphorylate Thr-916 in vitro (Chini and Chen, 2006), although it was later reported that Chk1 is not responsible for the phosphorylation of the CKAD in vivo (Bennett et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge supported by a citation to Chini and Chen, 2006.

claim: Chk1 is not responsible for the phosphorylation of the CKAD in vivo.
source: Chk1 kinase was reported to phosphorylate Thr-916 in vitro (Chini and Chen, 2006), although it was later reported that Chk1 is not responsible for the phosphorylation of the CKAD in vivo (Bennett et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge supported by a citation to Bennett et al., 2008.

claim: Casein kinases can phosphorylate in vitro the critical threonine residue in CKBD.
source: They showed that casein kinases can phosphorylate in vitro the critical threonine residue in CKBD, and that casein kinase γ1, among different types of casein kinases, promotes phosphorylation of CKBD in vivo and its depletion reduced phosphorylation of Thr-916 of the CKBD polypeptide (899-953) ectopically expressed in human cells, and diminished checkpoint activation.
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge from Dunphy's group (Meng et al., 2011).

claim: Casein kinase γ1 promotes phosphorylation of CKBD in vivo.
source: They showed that casein kinases can phosphorylate in vitro the critical threonine residue in CKBD, and that casein kinase γ1, among different types of casein kinases, promotes phosphorylation of CKBD in vivo and its depletion reduced phosphorylation of Thr-916 of the CKBD polypeptide (899-953) ectopically expressed in human cells, and diminished checkpoint activation.
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge from Dunphy's group (Meng et al., 2011).

claim: Depletion of CK1γ1 reduced phosphorylation of Thr-916 of the CKBD polypeptide (899-953) ectopically expressed in human cells.
source: They showed that casein kinases can phosphorylate in vitro the critical threonine residue in CKBD, and that casein kinase γ1, among different types of casein kinases, promotes phosphorylation of CKBD in vivo and its depletion reduced phosphorylation of Thr-916 of the CKBD polypeptide (899-953) ectopically expressed in human cells, and diminished checkpoint activation.
evidence: This is stated as prior knowledge from Dunphy's group (Meng et al., 2011).

claim: HCT116-323 is a derivative of HCT116 in which the promoter of Cdc7 gene is mutated.
source: Here, through CRISPR/Cas9 system, we have established a derivative of HCT116 (human colon cancer cell line) in which the promoter of Cdc7 gene is mutated. This cell line (HCT116-323), expressing Cdc7 at a low level, replicates its DNA at a normal rate, but replication checkpoint activation was significantly reduced.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: HCT116-323 expresses Cdc7 at a low level.
source: This cell line (HCT116-323), expressing Cdc7 at a low level, replicates its DNA at a normal rate, but replication checkpoint activation was significantly reduced.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1C.

claim: HCT116-323 replicates its DNA at a normal rate.
source: This cell line (HCT116-323), expressing Cdc7 at a low level, replicates its DNA at a normal rate, but replication checkpoint activation was significantly reduced.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1A and 1B.

claim: Replication checkpoint activation was significantly reduced in HCT116-323.
source: This cell line (HCT116-323), expressing Cdc7 at a low level, replicates its DNA at a normal rate, but replication checkpoint activation was significantly reduced.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1C.

claim: The AP (acidic patch) motif near the C-terminus of Claspin interacts with Cdc7.
source: The AP (acidic patch) motif near the C-terminus of Claspin interacts with Cdc7 and is required for Cdc7-mediated phosphorylation of Claspin and also for its interaction with various replication proteins.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the results section, referencing prior work (Yang et al., 2016).

claim: The AP motif is required for Cdc7-mediated phosphorylation of Claspin.
source: The AP (acidic patch) motif near the C-terminus of Claspin interacts with Cdc7 and is required for Cdc7-mediated phosphorylation of Claspin and also for its interaction with various replication proteins.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the results section, referencing prior work (Yang et al., 2016).

claim: The APDE/A mutant of Claspin does not interact with Cdc7.
source: We have generated a DE/A mutant (APDE/A) of Claspin, in which all the acidic residues in aa988-1086 were replaced by alanine, and have shown that this mutant does not interact with Cdc7 and is not phosphorylated by Cdc7 in spite of the presence of all the serine/threonine residues.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by prior work (Yang et al., 2016).

claim: The APDE/A mutant is not phosphorylated by Cdc7 in spite of the presence of all the serine/threonine residues.
source: We have generated a DE/A mutant (APDE/A) of Claspin, in which all the acidic residues in aa988-1086 were replaced by alanine, and have shown that this mutant does not interact with Cdc7 and is not phosphorylated by Cdc7 in spite of the presence of all the serine/threonine residues.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by prior work (Yang et al., 2016).

claim: APDE/A is not able to activate Chk1 in response to HU.
source: We found that APDE/A is not able to activate Chk1 in response to HU, and cannot bind to Chk1 in spite of the presence of intact CKBD sequence.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by Figure 2B and 2C.

claim: APDE/A cannot bind to Chk1 in spite of the presence of intact CKBD sequence.
source: We found that APDE/A is not able to activate Chk1 in response to HU, and cannot bind to Chk1 in spite of the presence of intact CKBD sequence.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by Figure 2A.

claim: A number of phosphorylation sites were identified near CKBD through mass spectrometry analyses, including S945 in CKBD.
source: Through mass spectrometry analyses, a number of phosphorylation sites were identified near CKBD, including S945 in CKBD.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4.

claim: Cdc7 depletion resulted in loss of most phosphorylations near CKBD including S945.
source: Cdc7 depletion resulted in loss of most of these phosphorylations including S945.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by Figure 4.

claim: Complete suppression of Chk1 activation requires depletion of both Cdc7 and CK1γ1 in all the cell lines tested.
source: We noted that complete suppression of Chk1 activation requires depletion of both Cdc7 and CK1γ1 in all the cell lines tested.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by Figure 5.

claim: Cancer cells expressing a high level of Cdc7 exhibit higher dependency on Cdc7 for Chk1 kinase activation.
source: The dependency of Chk1 kinase activation on each kinase differs between cancer cells and non-cancer cells; cancer cells expressing a high level of Cdc7 exhibit higher dependency on Cdc7, whereas non-cancer cells with a lower level of Cdc7 depend more on Chk1γ1.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by Figures 5 and 7.

claim: Non-cancer cells with a lower level of Cdc7 depend more on CK1γ1 for Chk1 kinase activation.
source: The dependency of Chk1 kinase activation on each kinase differs between cancer cells and non-cancer cells; cancer cells expressing a high level of Cdc7 exhibit higher dependency on Cdc7, whereas non-cancer cells with a lower level of Cdc7 depend more on Chk1γ1.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by Figures 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claim: Either Cdc7 or CK1γ1 can phosphorylate CKBD for checkpoint activation.
source: We propose that either Cdc7 or CK1γ1 can phosphorylate CKBD for checkpoint activation, while the cellular context affects the pathway choice in different cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental findings in Figures 5, 6, and 7.

claim: The cellular context affects the pathway choice for CKBD phosphorylation in different cells.
source: We propose that either Cdc7 or CK1γ1 can phosphorylate CKBD for checkpoint activation, while the cellular context affects the pathway choice in different cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental findings in Figures 5, 6, and 7.

claim: In HCT116, Chk1 activation was detected at 15 min after addition of 2 mM HU, and increased up to 50 min.
source: In the human colon cancer cell line, HCT116, Chk1 activation was detected at 15 min after addition of 2 mM HU, and increased up to 50 min.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: At 48 hr after transfection of Cdc7 siRNA, Cdc7 expression was reduced by over 90% in HCT116.
source: At 48 hr after transfection of Cdc7 siRNA, Cdc7 expression was reduced by over 90%.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Chk1 activation was reduced by ~90% at 30 min in Cdc7-depleted HCT116 cells compared to the parental cells.
source: Under this condition, Chk1 activation was reduced by ~90% at 30 min compared to the parental cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The growth of HCT116-323 was slightly slower than the parent.
source: The growth of HCT116-323 was slightly slower than the parent (data not shown), but the DNA synthesis or S phase progression was not noticeably affected.

claim: The DNA synthesis or S phase progression was not noticeably affected in HCT116-323.
source: The growth of HCT116-323 was slightly slower than the parent (data not shown), but the DNA synthesis or S phase progression was not noticeably affected.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1A and 1B.

claim: There was no significant difference in the level of BrdU incorporation between HCT116 and HCT116-323.
source: There was no significant difference in the level of BrdU incorporation (Figure 1A), and S phase proceeded in a similar timing for up to 8 hr after release from the double thymidine block.

claim: S phase proceeded in a similar timing for up to 8 hr after release from the double thymidine block in HCT116 and HCT116-323.
source: There was no significant difference in the level of BrdU incorporation (Figure 1A), and S phase proceeded in a similar timing for up to 8 hr after release from the double thymidine block.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1B.

claim: At 10 hr after release from double thymidine block, the wild-type HCT116 cells proceeded to G1, while HCT116-323 cells have not divided yet.
source: However, at 10 hr after release, the wild-type HCT116 cells proceeded to G1, while HCT116-323 cells have not divided yet (Figure 1B).

claim: HCT116-323 cells have some difficulty going through mitosis, although eventually they enter mitosis.
source: This suggests that HCT116-323 cells have some difficulty going through mitosis, although eventually they enter mitosis.

claim: The Cdc7 protein level was reduced by 90% in HCT116-323 compared to the parent HCT116.
source: The Cdc7 protein level was reduced by 90% in HCT116-323 compared to the parent HCT116.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1C.

claim: After HU treatment, Chk1 activation was reduced by about 80% at 30 min in HCT116-323 compared to the parent.
source: After HU treatment, Chk1 activation was reduced by about 80% at 30 min in HCT116-323 compared to the parent (Figure 1C), confirming that a certain level of Cdc7 activity is required for full activation of Chk1 in HCT116.

claim: A certain level of Cdc7 activity is required for full activation of Chk1 in HCT116.
source: After HU treatment, Chk1 activation was reduced by about 80% at 30 min in HCT116-323 compared to the parent (Figure 1C), confirming that a certain level of Cdc7 activity is required for full activation of Chk1 in HCT116.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the data in Figure 1C.

claim: Chk1 was co-pulled down with the wild-type Claspin and ST5A and ST19A mutants.
source: Whereas Chk1 was co-pulled down with the wild-type and ST5A and ST19A, it was not pulled down with ST27A (Figure 2A, lanes 8, 10–12).

claim: Chk1 was not pulled down with ST27A Claspin mutant.

claim: The acidic patch (AP; aa988-1086) of Claspin is required for its interaction with Cdc7 kinase.

claim: APDE/A fails to support phosphorylation of Mcm in non-cancer cells.
source: The DE/A mutant of AP (APDE/A) in which all the acidic residues in AP were replaced with alanine is deficient in interaction with Cdc7 and fails to support phosphorylation of Mcm in non-cancer cells (Yang et al., 2016).

claim: APDE/A mutant did not cause defect in phosphorylation of Mcm in cancer cells.

claim: The wild-type Claspin could restore Chk1 phosphorylation in Claspin-depleted MEF cells.

claim: The APDE/A mutant did not restore Chk1 activation in Claspin-depleted MEF cells.

claim: The wild-type Claspin could restore the Chk1 phosphorylation in Claspin-depleted U2OS cells.

claim: The APDE/A mutant did not fully restore Chk1 phosphorylation in Claspin-depleted U2OS cells.

claim: APDE/A is not phosphorylated by Cdc7 in vivo as well as in vitro.

claim: Cdc7-mediated phosphorylation of Claspin is required for checkpoint activation.
